analysis.title: Tech Rotation / BoE Ahead / Japan / RBA / Oil
key_insights: Post-election bounce is broad outside Tech, with a sharp unwind in momentum and semiconductors as investors rotate toward quality and defensive growth. The debate is whether the midterms pulled the AI capacity 'peak in 2028/29' discussion forward to 2027.

Tighter data-center restrictions could push hyperscalers to accelerate capacity, power and permits, pulling spend into 2027 but raising the risk of an earlier rollover in semis EPS revisions. The constructive case is that regulation elongates the cycle.
Flows favour hyperscalers over neoclouds. The UBS cash desk is a better buyer of hyperscalers and semi-cap equipment and better for sale in memory.
Selective buying in Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Lam Research. Intel, ServiceNow, CoreWeave, AMD and Sandisk are better for sale.
UBXXVOLT (AI Power) fell to a 52-week low as Texas stays in focus and investors price more regulatory and execution risk.
Macro tape cushioned indices: oil down about 10% with Brent near $93/bbl, DXY 40bp lower and yields falling.
Some excess positioning in semis and AI looks to be clearing, and Wednesday's washout may be close to pricing the risk. Friday's nonfarm payrolls is the main remaining macro catalyst this week.

Keith Parker says about 30% of 2028 data center additions are at risk, including 18 GW in Texas. Semis valuations are near multi-year lows and hyperscaler cloud revenue growth is strong. Buybacks are expected to accelerate with positioning light.

Five CTA buy triggers were crossed and SPX dealer gamma turned positive after three negative days. SPY rallied 1.7% with $60 bn of S&P 500 excess buying, almost all in the first 45 minutes. After 10:15am excess buying slowed to $2 bn and Nasdaq saw $17 bn of excess selling.
Into Thursday the main counterweight is risk-control supply: an estimated $15-20 bn of the $40-55 bn sell rebalance is done, leaving $25-35 bn of residual selling.

Hedge funds made their third-largest reduction in market exposure this year, leaving net exposure near five-year lows. UBS sees scope for an equity rally into year-end. A Democratic sweep is likely to boost Treasuries as divided government implies gridlock.
UBS expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.0% Thursday with a 7-2 vote (Dhingra and Taylor holding), then pause in December and hike once more in February to 4.25%, more dovish than the market.
BoJ minutes show members saw a need for further tightening, and one said the bank may need to accelerate hikes if prices deviate upward. The policy rate is 1.25% and markets expect a December hike.

RBA board members criticised Deputy Governor Hauser for signalling a hike before the meeting, after a 6-3 vote to lift rates to 4.85%. The desk says AUDUSD at 0.7035-0.7045 should be difficult resistance.
South Korea's September current account surplus hit a record $61.46 bn on chip exports, which rose 92.4% y/y to $130.72 bn.
UBS APAC tech view: AI infrastructure demand stays strong into 2027, with capex expected to moderate from 2028. Taiwan coverage trades at 14.7x next year's earnings.
UBS expects Banxico to cut 25bp to 6.25% Thursday, against only 5 of 30 surveyed economists. BNM is expected to hold at 2.75%.
UBS FX strategy sees no clean USD catalyst from the midterms and prefers EURUSD downside. Gold above 4,000 looks like a relief rally, and renewed oil strength could reverse it.
Japan: the desk favours buying a USDJPY pullback into 157.15-157.25, with resistance at 158.65-158.75.
Rates: 10y fell 8bp to 4.885% and 5s30s steepened 3bp to 59.2bp. Gasoline futures fell about 20c and the 1y zero-coupon inflation swap fell 23.5bp to 2.16%.
ARM fell 3.8% against about 10.4% implied move after a royalty revenue miss and no increase to the AGI CPU target, despite a headline beat.

ARM Q2 royalty revenue reported $670 mn vs $707.3 mn estimate. License and other revenue reported $773 mn vs $659.1 mn expected.

ARM Q3 guidance: revenue $1.49-1.59 bn and EPS $0.52-0.60, bracketing consensus of $1.52 bn and $0.55. Management reiterated up to $2 bn of AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028 without raising it.
AMD on Tuesday projected 2027 revenue growth of 80%, and Super Micro reinforced the AI infrastructure outlook per UBS APAC tech views.
